name: Grosser Aletschgletscher

tier.2016: extrapolated back from the 2017 survey at the cell scale of the first segment; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)
tier.2017: measured: swissALTI3D 2019 edition (survey 2017), placed at 2017-09-21; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)
tier.2018: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the lidar (60 % of the ice cells) and the 2023 survey with the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per 100 m elevation band; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots); stakes: 1 stake-years, model change = 0.89 of the reading (computed)
tier.2019: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the lidar (60 % of the ice cells) and the 2023 survey with the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per 100 m elevation band; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots); stakes: 1 stake-years, model change = 0.57 of the reading (computed)
tier.2020: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the lidar (60 % of the ice cells) and the 2023 survey with the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per 100 m elevation band; checked against ICESat-2: 334 shots, rmse 1.64 m (leave-one-granule-out); stakes: 4 stake-years, model change = 0.57 of the reading (computed)
tier.2021: measured: swissSURFACE3D lidar (60 % of the ice cells, computed; the flight days are in the lidar anchor); checked against ICESat-2: 283 shots, rmse 1.71 m (leave-one-granule-out); stakes: 3 stake-years, model change = 0.59 of the reading (computed)
tier.2022: interpolated between the 2017 survey, the lidar (60 % of the ice cells) and the 2023 survey with the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per 100 m elevation band; checked against ICESat-2: 121 shots, rmse 1.84 m (leave-one-granule-out); stakes: 4 stake-years, model change = 0.64 of the reading (computed)
tier.2023: measured: newest swissALTI3D edition (2024 edition, aerial images 2023), placed at 2023-08-10; checked against ICESat-2: 373 shots, rmse 1.38 m (leave-one-granule-out); stakes: 4 stake-years, model change = 0.77 of the reading (computed)
tier.2024: extrapolated beyond the 2023 survey at the cell scale of the last segment, from the smoothed difference of the surveys; checked against ICESat-2: 718 shots, rmse 2.40 m (leave-one-granule-out); stakes: 4 stake-years, model change = 0.70 of the reading (computed)
tier.2025: extrapolated beyond the 2023 survey at the cell scale of the last segment, from the smoothed difference of the surveys; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots); stakes: 4 stake-years, model change = 0.73 of the reading (computed)
tier.2026: estimate: extrapolated like 2024-2025, with the 2026 balance estimated from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch: provisional; checked against ICESat-2: 443 shots, rmse 3.10 m (leave-one-granule-out)

summary: Ice surface of each year 2016 to 2026 on the 3D strip: two swisstopo elevation models (2017, 2023), swisstopo lidar (25 tiles of 2021) and the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per elevation band for the years between and beyond. A model, not a measurement, except where a survey lies.

anchors.survey: Image strips over the strip in 2017 (swisstopo layer ch.swisstopo.lubis-bildstreifen): 2017-07-17 CRYOSPHERE MONITORING (40 % of ice cells, computed), 2017-08-07 CRYOSPHERE MONITORING (40 % of ice cells, computed), 2017-08-29 SWISSIMAGE (15 % of ice cells, computed), 2017-09-08 SWISSIMAGE (60 % of ice cells, computed), 2017-09-21 SWISSIMAGE (99 % of ice cells, computed). Which strip fed which cell is not published; the model puts the whole edition on one day.
anchors.placed_at: 2017-09-21 (a day a strip was flown, taken from the pair of flown days with the lowest ICESat-2 rmse (2.23 m); ties within 0.05 m go to the GLAMOS date if it is among them, else to the strip covering most ice. Chosen on the same shots as the check, so not independent)

anchors.source: swissSURFACE3D raster (swisstopo lidar DSM, 0.5 m, read at 20 m)
anchors.survey: GPS times of the point clouds of 26 tiles read (tiles with ice). 10 tiles hold at least 85 % of their points on a single day (2021-09-24 on 9, 2021-08-21 on 1); 15 tiles were flown on several days within 60 days and take the point-weighted mean day (uncertain by up to about a month); 1 tiles flown on days further apart (or not read) are not used. The lidar sits on 60 % of the ice cells (computed).
anchors.placed_at: the flight day of each tile (see above)

anchors.survey: Built from aerial images 2023: strips over the ice 2023-08-10 CRYOSPHERE MONITORING (32 % of ice cells, computed), 2023-08-10 DISASTER MAPPING (7 % of ice cells, computed), 2023-09-05 SWISSIMAGE (30 % of ice cells, computed), 2023-09-06 SWISSIMAGE (100 % of ice cells, computed). Which strip fed which cell is not published.
anchors.placed_at: 2023-08-10 (a day a strip was flown, chosen with A1 by the same pair rule)

shape: Between two anchors the surface follows the lowering of each elevation band, from snow-off (1 May plus Bw/|Bs| x 153 d, melt even from 1 May: an assumption) to 30 September. The band balance is the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletschgletscher itself (release 2025, 100 m bins from 1634 m, which cover the whole tongue; non-commercial); it only decides how the change between two surveys is spread over the years and heights, the size comes from the surveys. 2026 is not in release 2025: its glacier-wide balance is READ FROM THE GLAMOS FIGURE (winter +751.6 mm w.e., annual -3038.4 mm w.e., about +-100 mm w.e.) and spread to the 100 m bands with the figure's melt timing. Beyond the last anchor (2024 to 2026) the rate of the last segment is applied to the measured 2023 surface, from the anchor difference smoothed over about 100 m (the raw difference carries noise and made 2024 to 2026 rough). The ground outside the 2023 outline stays at its 2023 height and no fade is applied, so a step grows along the outline (median lowering of the ice cells next to it 2.6 m in 2024, 4.8 m in 2025, 7.8 m in 2026, computed). Every cell stays between its two anchors or, outside them, within 2.5 times the lowering of its band at the nearest anchor. The tip lake of 2024, 2025 and 2026 is flat at the level set earlier (an assumption: the real level is not known), with a raised rim.

validation.icesat2: ICESat-2 ATL06 v007: 2,272 shots on 2023 ice in 9 granules (July to October, slope under 20 degrees, quality 0, h_li_sigma under 1 m, inside the physical envelope). rmse 2.23 m over all years, bias +0.58 m (model minus shot), leave-one-granule-out: the A1 and A2 days are chosen on the other granules and the held-out granule is scored; with the days used 2.23 m. Per year (leave-one-granule-out): 2020 1.64 m (334 shots); 2021 1.71 m (283 shots); 2022 1.84 m (121 shots); 2023 1.38 m (373 shots); 2024 2.40 m (718 shots); 2026 3.10 m (443 shots). Years without summer shots are not checked.
validation.datum: Heights are corrected with a plane fitted on 10163 shots on stable ground outside the ice (NMAD 1.18 m).
validation.not_checked: The split of the loss between years is an assumption (even melt from snow-off to 30 September); ICESat-2 scores years with shots, not each year step. 10 of 82 ASTER AST14DEM scenes (NASA LP DAAC, July to October 2016 to 2026) passed the gate (rock NMAD at most 15 m, at least 300 rock and 200 ice cells) in 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022; ASTER is rough, so only differences of a few metres mean something. GLAMOS stake readings (25 stake-years, annual files, type 1, on modelled ice inside the 2023 outline) are a check of the year-to-year split: the modelled surface change is 0.68 of the stake reading on average (RMSE 1.05 m), as expected because stakes move with the ice.
validation.extended_area: Cells farther than 1 km from every ICESat-2 shot used for the check (8,148 of 49,849 modelled ice cells, computed) have no check; above 2,000 m swisstopo derives heights from stereo images (accuracy "1 to 3 m", swisstopo page).

bed: Ice surfaces are not allowed below the bedrock: swissBEDROCK (swisstopo, 10 m; under glaciers swissALTI3D minus a modelled ice thickness, GLAMOS 2020) is the floor.
not_used: Airborne DEMs of 2009, 2011 and 2017 (RAGMAC set; readmes say internal use only). The 2011 DEM is a composite with 2009 flights and DHM25 and sits above the ASTER thinning curve on the ice. Years before 2016 are not modelled: older pictures use the 2016 surface.
licences: swisstopo open government data (use, processing and commercial use allowed, source "Federal Office of Topography swisstopo"; terms page read 2026-10-30). GLAMOS balances: non-commercial (file headers). ICESat-2: used for checking only.
caveat_2026: estimate: extrapolated like 2024-2025, with the 2026 balance estimated from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch: provisional; checked against ICESat-2: 443 shots, rmse 3.10 m (leave-one-granule-out)

page.mapcap: The model area = the 3D strip (outlined in black), as set in the walkthrough. Blue: ice inside the 2023 outline, about 21.1 km² (computed, 20 m cells). Red dashed: every cell modelled as ice, including ground that was ice at the 2017 survey, about 23.1 km² (computed). The 2,272 ICESat-2 shots used for the checks are shown in the 3D viewer (last section). The ICESat-2 check covers the cells within 1 km of a shot; the rest, 16 % of the modelled ice cells (8,148 of 49,849, computed), follows the same rules but has no check. Pictures of years before 2016 use the 2016 surface (2016 is itself extrapolated back from the 2017 survey).
page.icesatNote: Also used to choose the survey days of both anchors, so not an independent check; the rmse is leave-one-granule-out (the days are chosen on the other granules).
page.asterNote: For scale: each used scene has a stable-terrain NMAD of 6.6 to 14.3 m (computed) (no used scene lies within 25 days of the 2023 anchor), so differences of a few metres are within ASTER's own scatter. rms = spread of the scene values of the year. Check only, not in the fit.
page.stakeNote: Over all 25 stake-years the modelled surface change is 0.68 of the stake reading (RMSE 1.05 m). Stakes read ablation of moving ice, so the model is expected to show a fraction. By year the ratio is 2018 0.89, 2019 0.57, 2020 0.57, 2021 0.59, 2022 0.64, 2023 0.77, 2024 0.70, 2025 0.73 (computed). Check only, not in the fit.

notes.uncertainty: Median over the ice of 2023, red whisker the 90th percentile (computed). The two swisstopo surveys carry 1.38 m (rmse of the 373 shots of 2023). The lidar of 2021 carries 1.43 m (rmse of 62 shots within 45 days of the lidar day). swisstopo quotes 0.5 m below 2000 m and 1 to 3 m above (as quoted by Bannwart et al.), so the true value may be larger on a tongue this high. Between and beyond the surveys the error grows with the size of the change (factors 0.12 and 0.20), calibrated on the same ICESat-2 shots, so it is not independent; where a year has shots it is not below their rmse. Years without shots (2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2025) rest on the formula alone. 2026 has no value on the chart: it is an estimate (its balance is estimated from a figure for Aletsch), and its map in the viewer adds 25 % of its increment (median 3.6 m).
notes.independent: ICESat-2 also chose the survey days of both anchors and calibrated σ, so it is not independent (rmse is leave-one-granule-out). ASTER scenes are checks only (10 of 82 scenes usable; usable years: 2016, 2017, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022). GLAMOS stakes (25 stake-years on modelled ice) are checks only. Click a year for the numbers.
notes.sharing: Solid: the GLAMOS annual balance of Grosser Aletsch per elevation band sets how the loss between two surveys falls into each year. Dashed: extrapolated beyond the last survey (2026 with an estimated balance); the years before the first survey are extrapolated back. Not used: measured years.

page.viewerText: The yearly surfaces in 3D with a year slider. Switch on ICESat-2 shots (what the model was checked against) and GLAMOS stakes (orange: stake, purple: automatic camera) and hover a record for its values. About 17 MB, loaded when you press the button.

bed.lead: Three checks on Grosser Aletschgletscher (all computed here, not source figures). The bed is the rock under the ice. "Radar bed" is the radar's own bed elevation (the survey surface minus the measured thickness, from the GLAMOS release); "model bed" is swissBEDROCK, which under glaciers is swissALTI3D minus a modelled GLAMOS ice thickness.
checks:
1 · Radar bed against model bed

At the 2,847 radar cells (20 m, median of the points in a cell), how far apart are the two beds?

Median −0.6 m over all cells, but it depends on the survey: +0.3 m (2011, 1,770 cells), −2.0 m (2009, 1,077 cells). Spread (standard deviation) 10.7 m in 2011, 9.8 m in 2009; over all cells 74 % are within 10 m and 99 % within 30 m.

Reading: the 2011 survey agrees closest (75 % of its cells within 10 m) and the 2009 survey least (71 %). This is not a validation: the model bed was made from these same surveys (GLAMOS 2020 model, Grab et al. 2021), and at the survey lines it is the measured bed.

2 · One survey against another

Where two surveys covered the same spot, how well do they repeat?

Only 243 spots (25 m cells) have two survey dates (2009 and 2011: 243). The beds implied by the two surveys differ by a median +5.8 m (later minus earlier) with a standard deviation of 20.9 m; 43 % agree within 10 m.

Reading: enough spots for a rough measure of how the surveys repeat.

3 · Ground that is ice free now

Radar points where the newest swissALTI3D shows ground, not ice: the exposed ground is the bed.

142 points (81 from 2009, 61 from 2011) on 5 flight profiles, ice about 79 m thick:

20092011
Radar bed − ground now+6.6 m (+4.3 to +8.5)+8.7 m (−1.0 to +19.1)
Model bed − ground now+0.5 m (−1.9 to +3.1)+2.7 m (−0.9 to +5.1)

Median, in brackets the middle half (years with too few points are not shown). 81 % of the points have the radar bed above the ground now.

bed.read:
What this supports

  • At the margins the radar bed lies 6.6 m above the exposed ground and the model bed 0.8 m above it (medians of the points of 2009, 2011).

What it does not show

  • Few places: the 142 points lie on 5 flight profiles, at the margins where the ice is about 79 m thick; deeper ice may behave differently.
  • No error band: the GLAMOS release has no uncertainty maps for the model bed, and swissBEDROCK's band under glaciers is about 0. Lakes, debris and the margin position (a few metres) were not screened.

How the points were chosen

  • In the 3D strip, at least 30 m outside the SGI2023 outline and 30 m inside the SGI2016 outline, so the model had ice there; newest swissALTI3D, slope at most 20°. With up to 30°: 195 points; with a 50 m margin: 12 points; with 100 m: none.
